charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Sumitomo Metal Mining Co., Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Sumitomo Metal Mining Co., Ltd.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Sumitomo Metal Mining Co., Ltd.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Sumitomo Metal Mining Co., Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Sumitomo Metal Mining Co., Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Sumitomo Metal Mining Co., Ltd.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Sumitomo Metal Mining Co., Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Sumitomo Metal Mining Co., Ltd.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue
segmentRevenue.content:
Sumitomo Metal Mining runs three reporting segments: Mineral Resources (equity stakes in copper/nickel mines -- Morenci, Candelaria, Sierra Gorda, Pogo), Smelting & Refining (copper, nickel and gold smelting/refining, including the Toyo and Harima plants and the Hyuga/Niihama nickel operations), and Materials (battery materials -- nickel sulfate and cathode materials for EV batteries -- plus electronic materials).

For Sumitomo Metal Mining Co., Ltd.: Smelting & Refining is by far the largest segment by revenue (it books the metal price as revenue even though treatment/refining charges are the real margin driver), so revenue scale alone overstates its contribution versus Mineral Resources' equity-method earnings. Materials revenue tracks EV battery demand and nickel/cobalt prices, not volume alone.

What to watch:

  • Smelting & Refining revenue swings are mostly copper/nickel/gold price, not throughput
  • Materials revenue growth or decline against EV battery demand cycles
  • Annual only -- the segment table is not broken out at the half-year

segmentProfit.title: Segment profit
segmentProfit.content:
The same three segments' profit contribution -- this is the better measure of where SMM actually makes money, since Smelting & Refining's large revenue carries thin treatment-charge margins while Mineral Resources' smaller revenue line (equity-method mine stakes) can contribute disproportionate profit at high metal prices.

For Sumitomo Metal Mining Co., Ltd.: Materials segment profit swung from +JPY13.8bn (FY2019) to -JPY54.2bn (FY2025) as nickel and cobalt prices fell and battery-material oversupply compressed margins, before recovering in FY2026 -- a reminder that the EV-materials bet is cyclical, not a steady grower. Smelting & Refining profit also went negative in FY2025 on smelting cost pressure and treatment-charge compression before recovering FY2026.

What to watch:

  • Mineral Resources profit as a leveraged play on copper/nickel/gold prices
  • Materials segment profit versus nickel/cobalt price and battery-material supply/demand
  • Whether Smelting & Refining can hold positive margin through a smelting cost cycle

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Sumitomo Metal Mining Co., Ltd.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Sumitomo Metal Mining Co., Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
